```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

The following code was adapted from Galloway et al. to model the predator-prey
dynamics of Pycnopodia and urchins under various outplanting scenarios.

The equations used in the model are:

dU/dt = i*U*(1 - U/K) - [p*q*U*S / (1 + b*U + c*O)]

dS/dt = e * [[p*Q*U*S / (1+b*U + c_o*O)] * [(1 - U/K)^z] + p*q*O*S / (1+b*U + c_o*O)] * [S/(S+g)]

Variable -> code
  U -> urchin           urchin density (prey)
  S -> pycno            sea star density (predator)
  O -> X1 + X2          alternative prey (susceptible + non-susceptible)
  i -> rec              fixed urchin recruitment
  K -> K_U              urchin carrying capacity (barren conditions)
  p -> rho_u            predator preference for urchins
  q -> alpha            predator search/attack rate
  b -> b_u              urchin saturation coefficient
  c -> c_o              alternative prey saturation coefficient
  e -> e                conversion efficiency of urchin biomass to Pycnopodia population growth
  g -> g                Allee effect threshold parameter
  z -> z                weight of nutritional impact
  d -> d                Pycnopodia mortality rate
  r -> r                Growth rate for alternative prey
  K_alt -> K_alt        Carrying capacity for alternative prey
  exchange -> exchange  exchange rate between susceptible/non-susceptible prey
  urchin_refuge -> urchin_refuge   urchin density largely protected from predation (physical refuge)

Load libraries

```{r}
library(deSolve)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

Instead of a `pars` list or global variables, `make_diffyq()` is a **factory
function**: you call it once with a full set of parameter values, and it
returns a ready-to-use ODE function that has those values "baked in" via
lexical scoping (a closure). Each closure is self-contained -- calling
`make_diffyq()` again with different values does not affect any
previously-created version, which makes this safe to use in loops or in
parallel.

```{r}
# Smooth approximation to max(x, 0) -- used for the urchin refuge so the
# transition to "protected" urchins has no sharp kink, which can otherwise
# cause solver convergence issues (e.g. lsoda "corrector convergence failed
# repeatedly") right around the refuge boundary. Higher `sharpness` makes
# this behave more like a hard cutoff; lower values transition more gradually.
smooth_floor <- function(x, sharpness = 5) {
  (x + log1p(exp(-sharpness * x)) / sharpness)
}
```

```{r}
# Defines a function with the model parameters as arguments 
make_diffyq <- function(alpha,        # search / attack rate (Q)
                         rho_u,       # preference weight for urchins (P)
                         rho_x,       # preference weight for alt prey
                         b_u,         # urchin saturation coefficient (b)
                         c_o,         # alt prey saturation coefficient (c)
                         rec,         # fixed urchin recruitment
                         K_U,         # urchin carrying capacity
                         e,           # conversion efficiency
                         g,           # Allee effect threshold
                         z,           # nutritional value exponent
                         d,           # sea star mortality
                         r,           # growth rate for alternative prey
                         K_alt,       # carrying capacity for alternative prey
                         exchange,    # exchange rate between prey pools
                         urchin_refuge # urchin density largely protected from predation
                         ) {

  # Returns this function below, taking arguments of t (current time),  
  # and N (current state vector)
  function(t, N, parms = NULL) {

    S <- max(N[1], 0)   # pycno density 
    U <- max(N[4], 0)   # urchin density 
    X1 <- max(N[2], 0)  # susceptible alternative prey
    X2 <- max(N[3], 0)  # non-susceptible alternative prey
    O <- X1 + X2         # total alternative prey

    # Urchins hiding in refugia (crevices, cracks) are largely protected
    # from predation. Uses a smooth threshold instead of a hard pmax() to
    # avoid solver convergence issues at the refuge boundary.
    U_access <- smooth_floor(U - urchin_refuge, sharpness = 5)

    # Pycno dynamics---------------------------------------------------
        
    # predator preference for urchins * attack rate * accessible urchin density *
    # predator density / (1 + urchin saturation * urchin density + alt prey saturation *
    # alt prey density) -- this is Holling Type II functional response (rate of 
    # prey consumption rises as prey density increases but levels off at some 
    # point when increases in prey density no longer increase consumption).
    # Only U_access (urchins above the refuge threshold) can actually be eaten.
    urchin_consumption <- (rho_u * alpha * U_access * S) / (1 + b_u * U + c_o * O)
    alt_consumption    <- (rho_x * alpha * O * S) / (1 + b_u * U + c_o * O)

    allee_effect <- S / (S + g)
    nutritional_impact <- pmax(1 - U / K_U, 0) ^ z
    birth_S <- e * (urchin_consumption * nutritional_impact + alt_consumption) * allee_effect
    death_S <- d * S
    dSdt <- birth_S - death_S

    # Urchin dynamics---------------------------------------------------------
    growth_U   <- rec * U * (1 - U / K_U)
    predation_U <- urchin_consumption
    dUdt <- growth_U - predation_U

    # Alternative prey ---------------------------------------------------------
    recx <- r * (X1 + X2) * (1 - (X1 + X2) / K_alt)
    predation_X1 <- (rho_x * alpha * X1 * S) / (1 + b_u * U + c_o * O)
    predation_X2 <- (rho_x * alpha * X2 * S) / (1 + b_u * U + c_o * O)
    dx1dt <- 0.5 * recx + exchange * (X2 - X1) - predation_X1
    dx2dt <- 0.5 * recx + exchange * (X1 - X2) - predation_X2

    return(list(c(dSdt, dx1dt, dx2dt, dUdt)))
  }
}
```

Parameterization 

```{r}
default_alpha         <- 2.5      # Galloway et al. uses alpha = 1000
default_rho_u         <- 1
default_rho_x         <- 1
default_b_u           <- 0.1
default_c_o           <- 0.1
default_rec           <- 1
default_K_U            <- 16.65
default_e              <- 0.01
default_g              <- 0.01
default_z              <- 0.3
default_d              <- 0.03      
default_r              <- 0.5
default_K_alt          <- 30
default_exchange       <- 0.1
default_urchin_refuge  <- 2       # urchin density protected from predation (~12% of K_U)
```

Running the model

```{r}
# Runs function 
run_mods <- function(P0, 
                      g             = default_g,
                      d             = default_d,
                      z             = default_z,
                      rec           = default_rec,
                      K_U           = default_K_U,
                      alpha         = default_alpha,
                      rho_u         = default_rho_u,
                      rho_x         = default_rho_x,
                      b_u           = default_b_u,
                      c_o           = default_c_o,
                      e             = default_e,
                      r             = default_r,
                      K_alt         = default_K_alt,
                      exchange      = default_exchange,
                      urchin_refuge = default_urchin_refuge,
                      X0            = 30,
                      Y0            = 10,  # initial urchin density
                      n_iter        = 500,
                      interval      = 1) {

  # Build a self-contained ODE function for this specific parameter set
  diffyq <- make_diffyq(
    alpha = alpha, rho_u = rho_u, rho_x = rho_x, b_u = b_u, c_o = c_o,
    rec = rec, K_U = K_U, e = e, g = g, z = z, d = d,
    r = r, K_alt = K_alt, exchange = exchange, urchin_refuge = urchin_refuge
  )

  # Run ODE  (state order: S, X1, X2, U)
  out <- ode(
    y     = c(P0, X0, X0, Y0),
    times = seq(0, (n_iter - 1) * interval, by = interval),
    func  = diffyq,
    parms = NULL,
    atol  = 1e-6,
    rtol  = 1e-6
  )

  data.frame(
    time   = out[, 1],
    pycno  = out[, 2],
    X1     = out[, 3],
    X2     = out[, 4],
    urchin = out[, 5],
    P0     = P0,
    g      = g,
    d      = d,
    z      = z
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run scenarios
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
P0_vals <- c(0.0001, exp(seq(log(0.001), log(0.06), length.out = 18)))
g_vals  <- c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.03)

results <- expand.grid(P0 = P0_vals, g = g_vals) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do(run_mods(
    P0     = .$P0,
    g      = .$g,
    n_iter = 500
  )) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Plot results

```{r}
results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    P0_label = paste0("P0 = ", round(P0, 4)),
    g_label  = factor(g, labels = c("No Allee (g=0)",
                                     "Weak (g=0.001)",
                                     "Moderate (g=0.01)",
                                     "Strong (g=0.03)"))
  )

results_long <- results %>%
  select(time, pycno, urchin, P0, P0_label, g_label) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols      = c(pycno, urchin),
               names_to  = "species",
               values_to = "density") %>%
  mutate(species = recode(species,
                          "pycno"  = "Pycnopodia density",
                          "urchin" = "Purple urchin density"))

p_updated <- ggplot(results_long,
                    aes(x = time, y = density,
                        colour = P0, group = P0_label)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    trans   = "log10",
    name    = expression(paste("Starting pycno density (", m^-2, ")")),
    breaks  = c(0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.06),
    labels  = c("0.0001", "0.001", "0.01", "0.06 (historical)")
  ) +
  facet_grid(species ~ g_label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = expression(paste("Density (no. ", m^-2, ")"))
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

p_updated
```

```{r}
# Plotting alternative prey
results_alt <- results %>%
  mutate(
    P0_label = paste0("P0 = ", round(P0, 4)),
    g_label  = factor(g, labels = c("No Allee (g=0)",
                                     "Weak (g=0.001)",
                                     "Moderate (g=0.01)",
                                     "Strong (g=0.03)"))
  ) %>%
  select(time, X1, X2, P0, P0_label, g_label) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols      = c(X1, X2),
               names_to  = "prey_type",
               values_to = "density") %>%
  mutate(prey_type = recode(prey_type,
                            "X1" = "Susceptible",
                            "X2" = "Non-susceptible"))

ggplot(results_alt,
       aes(x = time, y = density,
           colour = P0, group = P0_label)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    trans   = "log10",
    name    = expression(paste("Starting pycno density (", m^-2, ")")),
    breaks  = c(0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.06),
    labels  = c("0.0001", "0.001", "0.01", "0.06 (historical)")
  ) +
  facet_grid(prey_type ~ g_label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Susceptible vs non-susceptible alternative prey across Allee scenarios",
    x     = "Year",
    y     = expression(paste("Density (no. ", m^-2, ")"))
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
```

Print equilbriums
```{r}
# Extract equilibrium values (mean of last 50 time steps)
equilibrium <- results %>%
  group_by(P0, g) %>%
  filter(time >= max(time) - 50) %>%
  summarise(
    pycno_eq  = mean(pycno),
    urchin_eq = mean(urchin),
    alt_eq    = mean(X1 + X2),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    g_label = factor(g, labels = c("No Allee (g=0)",
                                    "Weak (g=0.001)",
                                    "Moderate (g=0.01)",
                                    "Strong (g=0.03)"))
  )

print(equilibrium)
```
